heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. City Region is the Banjar City Region.
2. City Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Banjar.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government that is the authority of the region.
6. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
7. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
9. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs within the Regional territory.
11. Violence is any act against women and children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
12. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
13. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
14. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
15. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
16. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise.
17. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
18. Handling is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, and/or has occurred.
19. Service is an immediate activity and action carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical support activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
22. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is formed at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.

heading: Article 12

Article 12

1. Prevention of Violence against Children as referred to in Article 11 letter a is implemented by:a. forming a network in efforts to Prevent Violence against Children;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Violence Prevention based on partnership patterns with the community, private sector and Non-Governmental Organizations; andc. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.

heading: Article 15
CHAPTER V
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 17

1. The City Regional Government implements efforts to prevent violence against Women and Children in the form of:a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values against Women and Children; andc. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Women's Empowerment and Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
2. The City Regional Government is obligated and responsible to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of:a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving community elements; andb. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for Victims of violence.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

P2TP2A

Article 19

1. The provision of services to victims is carried out in an integrated manner by P2TP2A.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) may receive and send case referrals from or to other service units in a networked manner.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. P2TP2A provides services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house.
2. In the event that P2TP2A does not yet have a safe house as referred to in paragraph (1), victims are referred to other integrated service centers that have safe houses.

heading: Article 21
Article 22
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

FPKK

Article 23

1. In order to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence, FPKK is established.
2. FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. City Regional FPKK;
b. Sub-district FPKK; andc. Village FPKK.
3. Provisions regarding the procedures for establishment, organizational structure, and elements of FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 24
CHAPTER VIII
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. In addition to P2TP2A as referred to in Article 20, the community may form forums or groups at the sub-district and village levels that function as P2TP2A networks in the framework of implementing efforts to Protect Women and Children Victims of Violence.
2. The formation of forums or groups in villages as referred to in paragraph (1) may be facilitated by the Village Government.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND REPORTING

Article 27

Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting on the Protection of women and children victims of violence is coordinated by the Regional Agency in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. The Regional Agency in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection conducts monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of the results of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence activities on a regular basis.
2. Reporting of activity results as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted to the Mayor through the Regional Agency in charge of regional development planning.
3. The implementation of monitoring, evaluation and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) involves the forum for handling victims of violence against women and children in a tiered manner.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 29

1. Guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out by the Regional Agency in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; andd. monitoring and evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
4. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, financing, quality, control and supervision.
5. Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is carried out in accordance with laws and regulations. (6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is carried out regularly every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 30

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Banjar City.

Enacted in Banjar on December 7, 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Economic factors, social environment and technological developments have a major influence on the increase in acts of violence.

This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as an effort to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously owned potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families. Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector.

Community service is the front line when there is potential violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Paragraph (3) What is meant by "related parties" includes among others:
a. implementation of counseling in the legal field involving the police, prosecutors, district courts, religious courts, legal advocacy institutions and non-governmental organizations;
b. implementation of counseling in the health field involving the health office, regional general hospitals, and other health services;
c. implementation of counseling in the spiritual field involving the ministry of religion and religious leaders; and d. implementation of counseling in the psychology field involving psychological assistants and/or psychologists.

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by "medical services" is a form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.

Letter b What is meant by "medicolegal services" is treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

Letter c What is meant by "psychosocial services" is services provided by assistants in the context of traumatic recovery of the victim's condition including the provision of space and safe houses to protect victims from threats and intimidation.

Letter d What is meant by "legal services" is services for victims in undergoing legal processes.

Letter e What is meant by "social reintegration" is an effort to reunite victims with family members, substitute families/institutions, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Letter f What is meant by "economic independence services" is services for skills training and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
